Termux changed to %1$s (%2$s). Check that you updated it yourself, then tap Trust this version in Settings › Termux.
Termux is signed with another key than the one you trusted: it was reinstalled from another source, or replaced. Robot won\'t use it until you set it up again in Settings › Termux.
This Termux is signed with a public test key — anyone can make an “update” that installs over it. Switch to the F-Droid build (Settings › Termux shows how).
Robot records this version (%1$s, installed or updated %2$s) and runs commands in it again. If you didn\'t update Termux yourself, don\'t: uninstall it and install Termux from F-Droid.
It is the GitHub build: “Run anyway” stays off until you turn it on again for this version.
Robot forgets the Termux it trusted and turns Termux off. Check where this Termux came from, then Test it and Trust it in the checklist below.

1. Keep a copy of what you need from Termux\'s home (~): its files go with the app.\n2. Uninstall Termux and its plugins (Termux:API and the others): the GitHub and F-Droid builds can\'t update each other.\n3. Install Termux from F-Droid, open it once, then set it up here again.
Run anyway, I understand the risk
Off: Robot runs nothing in this Termux
On for Termux %1$s only: a new version asks again
Run commands in the GitHub build?

This Termux is signed with a public test key: anyone can make an “update” that installs over it, and Robot would then send your commands to it. Robot still pauses after any update and asks again. The F-Droid build doesn\'t have this problem.
Robot also checks once a week whether Termux has a newer version: it asks api.github.com and f-droid.org, and sends nothing about you. You can turn this off in Settings › Termux.
Once a week, and when you tap Check now: Robot asks Termux\'s releases on GitHub and F-Droid which version is newest

Update available: %1$s. Robot never downloads or installs apps; the F-Droid build gets its updates from your F-Droid app.
Your Termux is a year or more older than the newest release, %1$s.
The developers released %1$s; F-Droid hasn\'t built it yet (it usually follows within days).
The last check couldn\'t reach GitHub or F-Droid
Robot asks only api.github.com and f-droid.org, over HTTPS, as Robot/%1$s, with no account, cookie or anything about you. It never downloads or installs another app.

Shizuku runs commands with the rights adb has, started by Android\'s Wireless debugging instead of a computer. Do “Let Robot repair that itself” first: once Robot may write that one setting, it sets its speech recognizer again by itself after every restart, so you need Shizuku only once.

By RikkaApps, only from its own releases (github.com/RikkaApps/Shizuku/releases) or from IzzyOnDroid. To check it\'s genuine: its package is moe.shizuku.privileged.api, and its signing certificate, which an app verifier such as AppVerifier shows, is the one the Shizuku project publishes. Android then refuses any update signed with another key.

Settings › About phone: tap Build number seven times. Then Settings › System › Developer options › Wireless debugging (it needs Wi-Fi). In Shizuku, start it through Wireless debugging and pair it as Shizuku shows. After every restart of the phone, start Shizuku again this way.
In Shizuku: Use Shizuku in terminal apps › Export files, and pick Termux\'s home folder (Termux, in the file picker\'s menu). Then paste this line in Termux:
Copy the line to paste in Termux
In Termux, run %1$s once: Shizuku asks whether Termux may use it. Allow it. It answers uid=2000(shell).
Each fix\'s page has its command for rish: the same command without “adb shell”, as rish -c \'…\', with Copy. With Termux set up in Robot, Robot can send it to Termux for you.
Shizuku gives adb\'s power to every app you authorize in it: authorize only Termux, and stop Shizuku when you\'re done (Shizuku\'s Stop, or turn Wireless debugging off).
Copied. Paste it in Termux and press Enter.

Robot is a voice assistant that runs entirely on this phone. Its brain, its ears and its voice are models stored here, so it answers even without a connection.
There\'s no account and no sign-in. Robot goes online only when you ask for something that needs it, such as the weather, or when you turn on a feature that says so in this guide.

Each page says what a feature does, what stays on the phone, and asks whether you want it. A choice is saved as soon as you make it. Skip this step keeps the default; Finish later brings you back here from Home.
Your questions, answers, notes, history and settings stay in Robot\'s private storage on this phone. Robot has no analytics, ads or tracking, and turns off Android\'s cloud backup for its files.
Things Robot does for you on your phone, without an account; most of them work even offline. Say them after “hey robot”, or tap Talk to Robot.
Each example says whether it stays on the phone, or what goes online and when. The ones that need setting up are off until you turn them on.
On the phone: messages stay in memory only
On the phone, only once it\'s unlocked
Online only to send your search words and read up to 3 pages
On the phone; online only for a weekly check for a newer Termux
Online only to the helper you set up, when it\'s asked
« Transcris cette réunion », puis « résume cette conversation »
Robot writes the conversation down in English and French, for hours, labels who said what, then sums it up: an overview, decisions, to-dos, numbers and dates.
Who said what needs the speaker model: Settings › Conversation
Lay the phone flat between you and someone who speaks French. Each half shows and reads aloud what the other person said, English and Québec French.
Faster with the fast translation engine: Settings › Conversation
“Remember that I parked on P3 until tonight”, later “where did I park?”
Robot keeps it until tonight and answers from it. You see, edit and delete everything it keeps.
“Read my messages”, then “reply in French: I\'ll be there at six”
Robot reads your new messages from the apps you chose, translates one in another language, and shows your reply in French on a card. It goes when you tap Send.
Off until you turn it on: Settings › Messages
“Every weekday at 7, tell me the weather and my calendar”
« Quand je ferme mon cadran, lis-moi mon résumé »
Robot shows the routine on a card and saves it when you say yes. The morning brief can also play by itself after your alarm: the weather, today\'s events, your reminders and how many messages wait.
Morning brief: off until you turn it on, Settings › Routines
Swipe up from a bottom corner over any app and ask about what you\'re looking at: a long article, a recipe, an error message.
Needs screen sharing on: Settings › Assistant setup
“Search the web for tonight\'s Canadiens game”
Robot searches with the service you chose, such as your own SearXNG, reads a few pages and answers with numbered sources.
Off until you set it up: Settings › Web search
Robot runs your own backup script in Termux, after a Run, Edit or Cancel card, and tells you how it went.
Off until you set it up: Settings › Termux
In car mode Robot talks through your car, announces a new message and reads your reply back before it goes, and opens Organic Maps\' route home.
Off until you add your car: Settings › Car mode. Announcements: Settings › Messages
“Ask Claude …”, or the AI on your own computer
For a question Robot can\'t answer well, it hands it to the helper you set up. Your screen, a photo or what Robot read goes only after a tap.
Off until you set one up: Settings › Helpers
Robot\'s brain is Gemma 4 E2B, an AI model from Google that runs on this phone. Which build it gets depends on the phone\'s chip.
If it doesn\'t load on the TPU, Robot switches to the general build by itself. Download that one too, from the Model tab, to have it ready.
You can also download it later from the Model tab. Before a download this big, Robot asks whether to wait for Wi-Fi.
The model comes from Hugging Face, pinned to one version and checked before Robot uses it. Nothing you say goes there. Once it\'s here, Robot answers without the internet.

Speech recognition turns what you say into text, and a voice reads Robot\'s answers aloud. Both are models that run on this phone. Until they\'re here, you can type, and the phone\'s own voice speaks.
Robot says a sentence in the voice it uses now
Your voice becomes text on the phone and is kept in its working memory only. No recording is made. The models download once and are checked before use.
To open Robot with a swipe, your headset\'s button or your voice, Android needs it as your digital assistant.
Pick Robot in Android\'s Digital assistant app
Set Robot as the digital assistant
For “hey robot”, and to tell you if Android turns Robot off after a restart
Swipe up from a bottom corner
Works on the lock screen too
Stay the assistant after a restart
One setting, set once: with a computer (adb) or without one (Shizuku, through Termux). Settings › Advanced › ADB fixes
Ask “what time is it?”, then come back here

“Hey robot” is heard on the phone; nothing is recorded or sent. Once the phone is unlocked, Robot can see the screen you\'re on when you open it, to answer about it. On a locked phone it never reads the screen.

Every action has a level: Just do it, Ask first (a card you confirm or cancel), or Off. Texts, emails, calls, new events and freeing space ask first; timers, notes and the weather just happen. The defaults are set; change them here or later.
Say yes or no while a card waits; a tap always works
Just do it, Ask first or Off, one by one
Each action\'s level, cards and the lock screen as on a new install
A spoken yes never sends your screen, a photo or what Robot read to a helper: only a tap does. A card for a name Robot isn\'t sure of needs a tap too.
Cards show on the phone and nothing goes until you confirm. A locked phone can\'t tell who is asking, so there Robot answers questions and does only the actions allowed on the lock screen.
People, texts, email, calendar and notes
Robot drafts texts and emails, adds events and keeps notes. It never sends a text or an email itself: they open as drafts in your app, and you press Send.
To text or email someone by name, and to look up a number
To read your events and add new ones. Without it, your calendar app opens to add one
Who Robot knows besides your contacts, and what you call them. Import a contacts file (.vcf) from its menu
Notes: say “note: buy coffee filters”. Your notes are in the Notes tab, and in Robot Notes on your home screen.
Android asks for contacts and the calendar only when you tap Allow. What Robot reads there is used on the phone for the question you asked. Notes and People stay in Robot\'s private storage.
Robot can read your messages aloud, summarize and translate them, and help you answer, from their notifications. It\'s off until you turn it on, and then only for the apps you choose.
Starts with your texting app; choose others in Settings
Needed: three steps in Android\'s settings
In private headphones and in car mode, never on the phone\'s speaker

Messages stay in the phone\'s working memory only, never written to storage, and go nowhere unless you send a reply. Robot needs no SMS permission and reads no message history. By default, a reply goes only after you tap Send on its card.
Say “remember that …” and Robot keeps it, to use in later answers. It keeps only what you ask, or what you keep from a card, never anything from a message by itself.
Robot remembers what you ask it to
Use memory on the lock screen
Anyone who can talk to your locked phone could hear what Robot remembers

Memory is one file on the phone, encrypted with a key in the phone\'s secure hardware that works only while the phone is unlocked, unless you allow the lock screen. Something like a password is kept private: never spoken unless you allow it, never sent to a helper.
Robot gets the weather when you ask, and finds “the nearest pharmacy” for Organic Maps\' route. A home town is used when Robot can\'t tell where you are.

Only a place goes online, when you ask: to Open-Meteo for the weather (a town, or where you are rounded to about 1 km), and for “the nearest …” the words and your area to the map search server. No account, no key. Looking up a home town asks Open-Meteo once.
Robot writes down a conversation in French and English, translates it face to face as your interpreter, and summarizes it.
Each line in the other language (%1$s)
Start one from Home › Conversation, the Transcribe tile, or say “hey robot, transcribe this conversation”.

Transcripts stay in Robot\'s private storage on this phone and are never backed up; the audio is never kept. Speakers are told apart on the phone. The optional files download once and are checked before use.

The morning brief tells you the time, the weather, today\'s events, your reminders and how many messages wait. Turned on, it plays by itself after you turn off your alarm. Say “morning brief” any time to hear it.
When it runs and what it says
At a time, at the first unlock, or only when you ask
Make your own routines by voice, such as “every weekday at 7, tell me the weather and my calendar”. Robot shows each on a card and saves it only when you say yes.
Routines run on the phone. The brief goes online by itself only for the weather, from Open-Meteo; nothing about you is sent.

A long press of your headset\'s or car\'s voice button opens Robot. In car mode, Robot talks through your car with short answers, helps with calls and Organic Maps\' routes, and keeps what needs the screen for when you park.
Off: other apps get the button
Off until you add your car. Set it up later, with the car connected

Your headsets and cars are remembered by their Bluetooth name and address, on the phone. New messages are announced only in private headphones, or in the car while car mode runs, never on the phone\'s speaker.
For a question Robot can\'t answer well, it can ask a bigger AI: Claude, another company\'s model with your own key, or a model on your own computer. None is set up until you add a key or a server.
Not set up: set one up later

Until a helper has a key, Robot asks before going to it. Only your question goes by itself; your screen, a photo or what Robot read needs a tap. With a daily budget, US$1.00 by default: once it\'s reached, Robot asks first for the rest of the day.
Online only when a helper is asked, and only to that helper. Keys stay encrypted on the phone. Robot shows which helper answered and what it cost.
Web search is off until you set it up with a service you choose: your own SearXNG, Brave, Kagi, Mojeek or a public SearXNG. Robot then answers current questions with numbered sources.

Advanced: Robot can run your own scripts and short commands in Termux, the Linux terminal app. Every command shows a card first. Off until every step of its checklist is done. Robot then checks once a week for a newer Termux, and after Termux changes it pauses until you trust the new version; it never runs commands in the GitHub build, signed with a public test key, unless you choose to.

Web search sends only your search words: to the service you chose, and to Wikipedia for who, what and where questions (Encyclopedia lookups, a switch). The few sites Robot reads see the phone\'s IP address. Never your conversation, location, contacts or notes. Termux runs on the phone; what your own scripts do is up to them. Once Termux is set up, Robot asks api.github.com and f-droid.org once a week which Termux is newest, and sends nothing about you.
Robot finds its new releases on GitHub and installs one only after checking it.
Once a day, in the background
Pre-releases, to try new things early. They may have problems.
A bug or an idea, sent with the app you choose. Or write to hey@robot-app.ai
The update check asks GitHub for Robot\'s releases: GitHub sees your IP address and Robot\'s version, nothing else. Feedback leaves the phone only when you send it yourself.
Here\'s what\'s on and off now, and where to change each later.

All of this runs on this phone. Robot goes online only to download what you asked for, for the weather and map searches you ask for, to check for updates, and for the helpers and web search you set up. There\'s no account, and the people who make Robot receive nothing from your phone.
